usage: papers extract [-h] [-v] [--debug] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                      [--porcelain] [--doi-only] [-R] [-n WORD_COUNT]
                      [--fulltext] [--scholar] [--openalex] [--image]
                      pdf [pdf ...]

print the bibtex of PDFs, from the DOI found in the PDF (metadata or text) or
a full-text search; with --doi-only, the DOI only

positional arguments:
  pdf                   one or several PDF files

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -v, --verbose         say what papers does, step by step
  --debug               debugging messages, and the traceback of errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        colours and hyperlinks in the output: auto (default)
                        when the output is a terminal and the NO_COLOR
                        environment variable is not set
  --porcelain           output for programs (as git's): the standard output
                        has only the entries that the command added, modified,
                        renamed or removed, or found already in the library,
                        one per line: "added KEY", "modified KEY", "renamed
                        OLD NEW", "removed KEY", "existing KEY"; every other
                        message goes to the standard error
  --doi-only            print the DOI of the PDFs: the DOI of the PDF
                        metadata, otherwise the first DOI of the text whose
                        title (from crossref) appears in the text
  -R, --recursive       accept directories and scan them for PDF files
  -n, --word-count WORD_COUNT
  --fulltext            fulltext only (otherwise DOI-based)
  --scholar             use google scholar instead of default crossref for
                        fulltext search
  --openalex            (papers-rs) use OpenAlex instead of default crossref
                        for fulltext search (environment: PAPERS_MAILTO,
                        OPENALEX_API_KEY)
  --image               convert to image and use tesseract instead of
                        pdftotext
